reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its main theme is the creator's account and criticism of OneCoin, including his claim that he lost access to money and his reasons for calling it a scam. He also promotes a coin-resale service, asking interested viewers to contact him and stating a $10 listing fee, but the video does not establish a deceptive promise or fraudulent money flow for that service.

citations.quote: I'm no longer with OneCoin what so ever
tell the facts, tell what happened with my experience
I put over two thousand dollars into OneCoin back in the day.
I wasn't able to, I couldn't take my money out whatsoever.
they found out that I was talking badly about the coin

opening.argument: The video supplies a concrete action-and-payment pathway, not merely criticism. Viewers are directed to a “special website,” asked to provide their coin information, and offered a service that will sell their coins for a stated ten-dollar fee. The same destination is also presented as a place to buy discounted OneCoin. That combination makes the token transaction and the requested contact or website visit central to the pitch. A viewer is not simply being warned about risk; they are being steered toward an external money-and-asset exchange whose terms and execution are not independently established.

citations.quote: I have made this special website I want to put a link below
I'm going to collect all the username's and how many times it split.
We will sell all your coin for you At only a ten dollar
you're gonna be able to buy this coin at a fraction the price

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a warning does not eliminate its operative solicitation. The speaker does not merely describe an exit option; he directs viewers to a website, requests account-related information, charges a fee, and offers to broker the coin. The reference framing therefore understates the portion of the video that turns the audience's concern into a specific transaction pathway.

citations.quote: I have made this special website I want to put a link below
We will sell all your coin for you At only a ten dollar
I'm going to collect all the username's and how many times it split.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material establishes an advertised resale service and a fee, but it does not establish a deceptive promise, an invented withdrawal, or fraudulent money flow. The speaker expressly describes the service as selling viewers' existing coins and says the fee is ten dollars. A transaction offer can be ordinary commerce even when it appears inside a warning.

citations.quote: We will sell all your coin for you At only a ten dollar
We will list your coin for ten10 and sell it.

opening.argument: The video presents several risk signals around token participation: a claimed price increase from forty cents to about $6.90, a proposed way to sell the token, and an invitation to buy it at “a fraction the price.” Those signals place purchase and resale inside a volatile, poorly substantiated market narrative. The speaker also says the coin has no solid technology and that there is no mining, while still describing a buy-and-sell venue. A token promoted through dramatic price framing and an external marketplace gives viewers a participation route without reliable evidence that the quoted value or liquidity is real.

citations.quote: now it's supposedly like $6.90
you're gonna be able to buy this coin at a fraction the price
There is no solid technology Their is no external There is no mining of the coin
We will sell all your coin for you At only a ten dollar

rebuttal.rebuttal: The service is not isolated from the token pitch: the video pairs a dramatic token-price account with an offer to buy the same coin cheaply and a mechanism to resell it. Whether the speaker calls the coin worthless is not dispositive; the actionable question is whether viewers are given a purchase route amid price-based persuasion and unsupported liquidity claims.

citations.quote: now it's supposedly like $6.90
you're gonna be able to buy this coin at a fraction the price
no one wants this coin at all.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The price statement is explicitly presented as the speaker's past experience and is qualified by “supposedly,” not offered as a guaranteed return. The later language points in the opposite direction from appreciation promotion: he says no one wants the coin and offers to help people sell. The material therefore shows criticism and an attempted exit service, not a promise that buying will produce gains.

citations.quote: now it's supposedly like $6.90
because no one wants this coin at all.
Please contact me ASAP, let me help you get rid of this garbage coin

opening.argument: The warning format also functions as promotion for an alternative token transaction. After condemning OneCoin, the speaker gives viewers a direct commercial next step: contact him, use his website, sell their holdings for a fee, or buy discounted coins there. He emphasizes his own crypto involvement and repeatedly contrasts OneCoin with Bitcoin, which positions him as a gatekeeper for the audience's next move. The apparent investigation thus channels viewers toward a specific marketplace and token activity rather than ending with neutral information.

citations.quote: I'm no longer with OneCoin what so ever
now it's supposedly like $6.90
I have made this special website I want to put a link below
Please contact me ASAP, let me help you get rid of this garbage coin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The speaker's stated opposition is precisely what makes the promotion effective: viewers worried by the allegations are immediately offered his website and assistance with their holdings. The closing instruction to contact him is a conversion step, and the offer to buy discounted coins expands the commercial pathway beyond merely reporting personal experience.

citations.quote: you're gonna be able to buy this coin at a fraction the price
Please contact me ASAP, let me help you get rid of this garbage coin
I'm going to collect all the username's and how many times it split.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The material supports an exit-oriented service, not promotion of OneCoin as a profitable investment. The speaker tells viewers to get rid of it, calls it garbage, and says the service will sell existing holdings. His personal crypto background and a contact request do not establish that viewers are promised appreciation, dividends, or a deceptive token return.
